about.studioCaption: In the studio — studies of light and shadow
about.bio1: Born in Tielt, Belgium, in 1966. I now live and work in Ghent. My journey in the arts began with color pencils and grew into a lifelong exploration of visual expression. I earned a Master's degree in Art History from Ghent University, followed several years later by two years of Textile Design studies at KASK in Ghent. At the Royale Académie Internationale d’Été de Wallonie I immersed myself in the techniques of the old masters — optical mixing and working in transparent glazes — a study I have continued to deepen ever since through specialised studios and masterclasses.
about.bio2: My work is a personal and passionate quest to translate the fragility and the essence of life and nature into images. I create in dialogue with nature, drawn to the interplay between light and shadow, the infinite and the transitory, the dynamic and the static. In May 2026 I took part in a residency at Convento de Mértola (Portugal), working with Japanese paper and the rhythms of wind, light and shadow — a turning point that placed natural processes at the centre of my practice.
about.mediumPaintingDesc: Abstract and observational work inspired by nature. Oil works in progress look at light and ever-changing shadows; acrylic pieces such as Breathing in & breathing out (24 × 30 cm, 2022) explore stillness and breath on canvas.
about.mediumPhotographyDesc: I often choose watercolor and gouache for their delicate and fluid language — botanical studies, plants and florals, and pieces such as Vagues, Gigaro for World Oceans Day.
about.mediumTextileDesc: Textile remains a clear pillar of my practice — from Textile Design studies at KASK to works such as Weavings and Weavings II (acrylic on linen, incl. 100 × 120 cm, 2019). Tactility, woven surfaces and ecoprint on linen from residency research add a physical, layered dimension to my visual language.
about.approach: I work intuitively, translating impressions and emotions into visual form. My process begins with a sense of calm and focus — a counterbalance to the complexity of contemporary life. Whether I am painting in oil, building up layers of watercolour or studying shadows, my work seeks a space where attention can slow down and where the nuances of the image can gradually reveal themselves.
